newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sellers rush as German grain intervention closes.
newsitem.headline: Sellers rush as German grain intervention closes.

text.p: Some 87,189 tonnes of grain were offered into German intervention stores over the last week but offers last Saturday, as yet uncounted, may total up to another 100,000 tonnes, the state intervention board BLE said on Monday.

The November/May 1996/97 season officially ended at midnight on Saturday, May 31, showing an overall lower volume than seen in 1995/96 and sharply down from the millions of tonnes offered each year in the early 1990s.
"Saturday's last-minute offers will take a few days to evaluate," a BLE official said.
"They were probably prompted by uncertainty in the grain market, but it must not be forgotten that they may be withdrawn by the sellers or rejected by BLE on quality grounds."
Volumes offered between May 23 and May 30 included 42,529 tonnes of soft wheat, 16,480 tonnes of rye and 28,180 tonnes of barley.
Total grain volumes lagged those of last year.
By May 30, a total 1,304,435 tonnes had been offered compared with 1,660,239 tonnes a year earlier.
In 1996, the final May 31 figure was 1,674,858 tonnes, down from 3,674,458 tonnes as of May 1995.
Offers are defined as volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores.
The May buying-in price for all grains was 248.61 marks/tonne.
